project.name: sakura-call
project.description: Sakura Call is a private two-person Next.js WebRTC audio calling tool with English/Japanese transcription and translated subtitles, designed for on-demand local public testing through Cloudflare Tunnel and direct TURN fallback.

layers.name: Documentation and Product Constraints
layers.description: Project README, task list, and agent guidance that define Sakura Call as a private two-person audio-only communication tool.

layers.description: Client React components for language selection, display-name capture, in-room WebRTC controls, participant panels, and subtitle display.

layers.description: Shared browser/client utilities for audio segmentation, microphone enhancement, WebRTC setup, Socket.IO client creation, room-code persistence, and bilingual copy.

layers.description: Custom Node server, cookie parsing, in-memory room state, Socket.IO signaling, transcription, and translation services that power the live call.

layers.description: Runtime scripts and TURN/Cloudflare infrastructure that start the app for a call, expose HTTP through Cloudflare Tunnel, and provide direct TURN relay fallback.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README and constraints to understand the private two-person audio translation workflow and the on-demand operating model.

tour.title: Join and Host Flow
tour.description: Read the Next.js entry route to see how language, display name, owner unlock, room creation, and four-digit room-code joining are coordinated.

tour.title: In-Room Call Experience
tour.description: Follow the main call component and supporting panels to understand microphone permission, WebRTC audio, participant status, and translated subtitle display.

tour.title: Audio Capture and WebRTC Helpers
tour.description: Inspect the browser-side media helpers that enhance microphone input, segment speech into WAV chunks, and configure STUN/TURN peer connections.

tour.title: Server APIs and Room State
tour.description: Move to the custom server and room store to see owner authentication, rate limiting, room-code lookup, creator secrets, and the hard two-person room limit.

tour.title: Signaling, Transcription, and Translation
tour.description: Trace the Socket.IO signaling layer and OpenAI wrappers that turn incoming audio chunks into translated captions for the other participant.

tour.title: On-Demand Public Runtime
tour.description: Finish with the run scripts and infrastructure settings that start TURN, build the app with current relay configuration, expose HTTP through Cloudflare Tunnel, and clean up on exit.

tour.title: Build and Tooling
tour.description: Review package scripts and compiler/lint styling configuration to understand how the project is developed and verified.
